1 Introduction

Essentially, in this article we intrinsically employ two powerful methods: Bounding and Optimizing. In rough terms, in every example the goal is to find two ”almost equal” functions fnf_{n} and gng_{n} wrapping the function we are looking for, i.e,

fn​(x)≤f⁡(x)≤gn​(x)∀n∈ℕf_{n}(x)\leq f(x)\leq g_{n}(x)\quad\forall{n\in\mathbb{N}}

Then, by letting we can derive the closed form of .
In order to ”wrap” the function , we try to ”optimize” the bounds found on the step by bounding a side (either the left or the right) of the given functional by imposing the inequality of the step to each term. We simplify and hope that would be a better approximation for than .
Usually, the simply stated ”simplification” can be cumbersome and would be too technical to perform. This is when the supremum and infimum come in handy. More specifically, rather than following a ”bottom-up” approach, i.e., starting from and generating , we follow a ”top-down” approach, i.e., we assume that we have already found the functions 1 and that best approximate and proceed by contradiction. In other words, any other approximation for should be worse than the one given by , .
Furthermore, instead of ”globally” applying this method, i.e., searching for such that all obey the inequality, we can apply it ”locally”. In other words, we can search for such that:

for a particular and derive the limit and use it to find . In particular, when is a boundary point (e.g., for positive real-valued functions), the monotonicity of can connect the limit with the or the of .
Usually, the solution we expect is of the form , therefore, it is advisable to apply this method to and constants to deduce that or to calculate the limit , i.e, the derivative of at . Though at first glance the limit might not be as useful as the we have included in this article some examples that illustrate methods to harness the existence of the derivative to solve the problem, such as the derivation of a differential equation.
The concepts briefly mentioned previously and further explained in the following sections provide a broad toolbox for solving even intricate functional equations problems. I hope, therefore, that this article will not only communicate to the reader this toolbox but also bestow valuable insights for solving such problems.
